title: A codex seat can reach its MCP tools: the spawn surface stops handing it an approval policy of never
description:

A real `codex exec` seat spawns, registers, and is handed `MCP tool call requires approval, but approval policy is never`. It therefore can never call `work_get_context`, and so can never reach `review_submit` or `work_release`. NO CODEX SEAT CAN DELIVER ANY NODE. Everything upstream of the MCP call works: the fresh-store lane comes up, the seed reaches `READY node.deliver@node-live-livecodex2105097`, the provider is chosen by the DURABLE SETTING (`project.set_agent_provider` -> HTTP 200 `AGENT_PROVIDER_SET`, `MOE_AGENT_COMMAND` verified UNSET), and six durable `internal.wrapper.seat_start` rows carry `{"agentVersion":"codex-cli 0.153.4","provider":"codex"}` with live codex-shaped argv (PID 53332; node 40484 -> cmd 61832 -> codex).

SECOND, SMALLER FINDING, codex-side not a moe bug, record it rather than fixing it here: `--ignore-user-config` silently downgrades `--sandbox workspace-write` to `read-only`. Controls measured: user-config -> workspace-write; +ignore-user-config -> read-only; +ephemeral -> read-only (ephemeral exonerated); danger-full-access -> honoured.

WHY THIS ROW EXISTS RATHER THAN A DEPENDENCY EDGE: the findings sit on task-48932bec, which is already DONE, so naming it in blockedOnTaskIds would auto-unblock the waiters on a signal that fixes nothing. worker-ca28be90 said so explicitly and deliberately left blockedOnTaskIds empty.

SAFETY: any control that readmits user config must run with the real board's MCP server unreachable — a bare `codex exec` on this host has been measured calling the operator's own moe server unprompted. Choose the NARROWEST tier that produces a completed MCP call, and say in the note why each narrower one failed.

Buys neither finding. Not shipped.
(iv) `--dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox` — strictly wider, not shipped.

`--approve-for-me` WORKS (controls C2/G/H) but is REJECTED as the shipped form: it is mutually exclusive with `--sandbox` (control C: `error: the argument '--sandbox <SANDBOX_MODE>' cannot be used with '--approve-for-me'`), so shipping it would delete `--sandbox <role.sandbox>` from argv, erasing the CHAIN/CODING role distinction from the spawn surface and redding the e2e `toContain("--sandbox")` arm. CORRECTION TO THE PRIOR RECORD: `--ignore-user-config` is NOT the cause of the sandbox downgrade. With no config.toml loaded by ANY route (the flag, OR a scratch CODEX_HOME) `--sandbox workspace-write` banners `read-only`. With the host config loaded, control P banners `workspace-write` and control Q (no `--sandbox`) banners `danger-full-access` — the host config sets `sandbox_mode = "danger-full-access"`, so P was the flag NARROWING that, never the flag working from a clean baseline. Real rule: codex 0.153.4's `--sandbox` cannot raise the mode above the `read-only` default when no config.toml supplies `sandbox_mode`. `--ephemeral` stays exonerated (control F).

SECURITY MEASUREMENT, control O, to be written into the docblock not buried: under the shipped tier the sandbox gives NO CONTAINMENT. A seat with `--sandbox read-only` wrote to an absolute path OUTSIDE its workspace, banner still reading `sandbox: read-only`. `on-request` lets the model request escalation, `auto_review` grants it with no human, and the escalated command runs unsandboxed. Controls I and J confirm from the other side: `-c sandbox_mode=read-only` and `=workspace-write` give identical write outcomes, so the base mode is ADVISORY. EVERY tier measured that completes an MCP call also loses containment — this is the unavoidable price on codex exec 0.153.4, not a choice between a safe option and a wide one.
